x: Outstanding recollections of the meeting were a fine sprint double by Ivan Mayers, some grand half miling by J. Davies (1m.57.8) and B. Hallowell (1m.59) and a very good half mile by Charlie Dabbs.
Brian Hallowell won the 880 yards with George Davidson 3rd. We had only one runner in the mile, Steve Boreham, who did his fastest time in finishing 3rd.
The R.A.M.C. were unable to compete in every event, but in winning the 880 yards their runner Baker scored a fine win in 1m.58.5s. closely followed by B.

In the North Brian Hallowell won the Cheshire Mile championship. Down south Brian Morris was successful in Sussex in the 220 yards and 440 yards events, and Stan Vickers accomplished a Kent County best in the two miles walk in 14.27.

Brian Hallowell had a personal best when he won the first of the two 1 mile races in 4m. 15s. leading the whole way. Ron Holtum found he was unable to beat Shenton in the 100 yards final and galloping Charlie Jones amazed us by finishing 2nd in the 220yds.

Brian Hallowell won the mile in 4m. 21.5s. with John Davies 2nd and Ray Tooby 3rd. John took the lead with 220 yards to go but Brian fought back in the home straight and passed John a few yards from the finish.
The one mile heats saw some grand racing and Brian Hallowell was unlucky not to reach the final. His time of 4m. 11.2s. in finishing 3rd in his heat was only .6 of a second too slow.
Our John Davies and Brian Hallowell ran with rare judgment and proved that with wise training they are capable of giving the best a run for their money.
In the Sefton Branker Trophy Meeting on 25th July Brian Hallowell representing the Civil Service was 2nd in the mile and John Davies (Middlesex) was 3rd.
In Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Pat Newell and Brian Hallowell, to name but a few, we have runners of the class of which champions are made.
